limitations: Linux/local filesystem only; isolated format 1004; no migration, S3 backend, online backup, physical power-cut certification or production adoption.
All writers/checkpointers must participate; raw SQLite writers and physical-file manipulation are unsupported.
The 256 MiB item in each six-order FUSE sequence follows a timed 64 MiB write in the same new workspace. cold_256 separately measures a standalone 256 MiB write in a new workspace.
Native software I/O counts include setup/readback/close; directory fsync and device-internal traffic are not counted. The native timings are instrumented, unlike FUSE timings.
All stalls and failed development evidence are retained. Monitor counters include unrelated host activity and untimed cleanup; they cannot attribute device traffic to one candidate.
The deterministic loss model retains all SQL bytes and only successfully synchronized sidecar images; it is not a claim of hardware power-cut testing.
